quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because few vehicles will be coming.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
If a solid yellow line is next to your lane and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or curve. You cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers should use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles proceed in order of arrival at a four-way stop. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When must pedestrians yield to motor vehicles?

options.text: When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
When crossing in a marked crosswalk.
When the vehicle is a pickup truck.
Only in city limits.

questions.correctAnswerText: When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles when crossing without a crosswalk or intersection. They must also yield when a traffic signal tells them to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
Intersections are coming up.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on the road will end soon. Drivers in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: What conditions must be met to pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street, you need all three: clear visibility ahead, time to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a vehicle with enough speed to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop. A train or other vehicle may be using the tracks.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Enter the exit lane well before your exit. Start slowing down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What should a driver do if involved in an accident?

options.text: Stop at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Stay out of traffic lanes to avoid being hit. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay centered, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get attention. If the other driver does not move, steer right. Do not steer left—the other driver may correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow reduces the impact.

questions.question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: They are deaf.
They are a police officer.
They are blind.
They have poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and proceed carefully. Be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Take your foot off the gas, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the gas pedal and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road. Keep both hands on the wheel and make a small turn to enter the right lane. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says not to. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Driving at night compared to driving during the day is:

options.text: Safer.
About the same in danger.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Other cars' headlights can blind you. There are more tired or impaired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: A green arrow and red light together means:

options.text: You can only go straight.
You can only go in the direction of the arrow.
Wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only go in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights but with a crossbuck sign, you should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Lower your radio volume to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are certain no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions greatly affect how well you drive. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can make it hard to drive safely. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic light is broken.
You do not need to stop completely.
Road conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver will hit you, sound your horn to alert them.

questions.question: When driving in Idaho, you must:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive at a speed that is safe and appropriate for conditions.
Drive 10 mph below the posted speed limit at all times.
Always drive at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a speed that is safe and appropriate for conditions.
questions.explanation: Idaho law requires you to drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions. Slow down whenever conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means you can pass if it is safe. You may only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at a constant speed.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A good defensive driver watches what other drivers are doing and expects problems before they happen. This helps prevent crashes even if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: When must a driver yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the driver's side of the road.
If the pedestrian raises their hand to signal the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and let other traffic go first.

questions.question: What do studies show about wearing a seat belt properly?

options.text: It increases the chance of death in a crash.
It reduces damage to your car.
It reduces serious injury in a crash.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces serious injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Studies show that wearing a seat belt properly greatly reduces your chance of serious injury in a crash. Seat belts prevent 60 to 70 percent of deaths in car crashes.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicycles.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: When approaching a curve on a narrow road where you cannot see ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop, get out, and walk around the curve to see what is ahead.
Flash your headlights on and off several times.
Sound your horn and stay near the right edge while driving slowly around the curve.
Speed up to get around the curve quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn and stay near the right edge while driving slowly around the curve.
questions.explanation: On mountain roads with curves, if you cannot see ahead, sound your horn and proceed slowly while staying near the right edge of the road.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
May not turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction but you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the road. The broken line is next to your lane. When may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
If the road ahead is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can pass. You may cross the line to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when passing other vehicles?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrians may cross here.
Construction workers are on or near the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians may cross here.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign alerts drivers that pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The larger vehicle.
The car on the left.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed.
Road work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs are orange. They warn drivers of work areas ahead. Slow down and be ready for changes or hazards in a construction zone.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, when may you proceed?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop completely before entering the intersection. Check that it is safe, then proceed.

questions.question: You are turning left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Slowly edge into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: You are on the interstate and pass your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cross traffic to make the turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue to the next exit.
Back up to reach the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at an exit you missed. Continue driving and use the next exit.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a four-way intersection is ahead.
